chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the stipulation in slave girls that they should not be sold, nor inherited, nor gifted. So he said: That is allowed, except for inheritance, for she can be inherited, and every stipulation that opposes the Book of Allah is rejected.

key_terms.الْإِمَاءِ: Slave girls (plural of umm walad or female slave)

ai.seo_question: Can a master stipulate that his slave girl cannot be inherited?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'rad al-shurut' (nullification of contradictory conditions) in slave transactions, distinguishing between contractual stipulations and divine law. While parties may agree to restrict sale or gifting, the Imam clarifies that inheritance cannot be waived because it is a fixed right ordained by Allah, rendering any clause contradicting this divine mandate void.
